plans.note: Section 9 (Limitation of Liability) is the primary target; check mutuality, cap amount and whether indemnity (sec-8-2) and confidentiality (sec-10) breaches are carved out. Section 8 disclaimer may interact with the cap.
Section 8 INDEMNIFICATION should carry Commerce One's IP infringement indemnity in our favour as licensee/host; verify our reciprocal indemnity is narrow and that the sec-9 cap does not swallow it.

Watch the grant of rights and the CORIO MARKET SEGMENT / TERRITORY definitions for field-of-use or competing-product restrictions on us; sales and marketing cooperation (Exhibit D) may also limit which competing offerings we can promote.

Check whether the grant or the marketing cooperation exhibit makes Commerce One our exclusive source of e-procurement software or bars us from hosting rival platforms; the CORIO MARKET SEGMENT definition may be the vehicle.

Pricing, revenue sharing and payment terms are where any best-pricing or most-favoured-customer language would sit; only flag if the MFN runs against us (i.e., we must give Commerce One our best terms).

No dedicated non-solicit heading; if present it would be buried in Miscellaneous or near the personnel/support provisions. Confirm before marking missing, and note that absence favours us so no redline is needed.

Section 11 Term and Termination: check for a convenience right in our favour, notice period, any termination fee or accelerated payment in the fees/payment terms, and whether Commerce One can exit mid-term.
Auto-renewal term and non-renewal notice window should be in Section 11; any renewal price uplift would appear in Exhibit B pricing.

Governing law, venue and any arbitration (note the defined term RULES, which suggests arbitration rules are referenced) will be in Miscellaneous; verify California or another accepted forum and court access.
Assignment clause in Miscellaneous; confirm we may assign to affiliates and successors and that Commerce One has no termination right on our change of control (relevant given ASP business).

Grant of Rights plus the DEVELOPMENTS and EMPLOYEE NDA/INVENTION AGREEMENT definitions are the likely ownership provisions; check that our customer data, configurations and paid-for developments do not vest in Commerce One, and review trademark and escrow sections for related IP terms.

Section 2 Grant of Rights read with the SOFTWARE, DEMONSTRATION SOFTWARE, TERRITORY, CUSTOMER(S) and CORIO SERVERS definitions and Exhibit A; confirm sublicensing to our hosted Customers, affiliate/contractor coverage and that the licence is not revocable at will.
Given revenue-sharing fees, expect a records-inspection/audit right over our books in the fees or payment terms sections; test frequency, notice, on-site scope and who bears cost.
Look for late-payment interest, shortfall payments or penalty-style amounts payable by us in Fees/Payment Terms; service credits running to us are acceptable and should not be flagged.

Section 7 Warranties and Disclaimer plus the Acceptance Test and Warranty Period definitions; assess warranty duration, remedy adequacy and the breadth of the disclaimer, with Exhibit C support obligations as the ongoing remedy.
No insurance heading in the outline; check Miscellaneous and the indemnity section before recording as missing, and calibrate the ask to Commerce One's limited access to our data.

Exhibit B pricing and revenue-sharing fees are the likely home of any minimum guarantee, seat commitment or take-or-pay; check whether termination rights in Section 11 provide an exit from any such commitment.

Effects-of-termination language in Section 11 plus the Source Code Escrow in Section 12; confirm continuity for our hosted Customers, data/materials return and any wind-down or migration assistance period.
